title: CUDA runtime/driver mismatch breadcrumbs (personal scratchpad)
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad while debugging recurring GPU OOM / driver mismatch issues on local dev workstation and in a container. Not polished — notes, commands, outputs, hypotheses, next steps.

SYMPTOMS:
- Intermittent CUDA failures when starting inference server in container: "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" and occasional OOMs during model load even with small batch sizes.
- CPU-only fallback sometimes occurs (torch reports no CUDA).
- Host nvidia-smi shows GPUs but container reports no devices or throws runtime errors.

ENVIRONMENT (host):
- Ubuntu 22.04 (WSL2 for laptop case, separate desktop with native Linux).
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX A5000 (driver tested: 525.89.02 on desktop), laptop MX450 on WSL2.
- CUDA toolkit in conda env: cudatoolkit=11.7 (conda), also have system CUDA 12.1 installed in /usr/local/cuda-12.1.
- PyTorch: 2.2.0 built with cu117 (pip wheel).
- Container runtime: docker 24.x with nvidia-container-toolkit 1.11.0.

COMMANDS TRIED (host & container) and OUTPUT SNIPPETS:
1) Check driver + runtime on host:
$ nvidia-smi
Tue Nov 28 11:03:01 2024
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.89.02    Driver Version: 525.89.02    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
|  0   RTX A5000    Off          | 00000000:01:00.0 Off |                  N/A |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Note: nvidia-smi reports CUDA Version: 12.1 (driver supports up to 12.1) but conda env uses cudatoolkit 11.7. That mismatch is usually OK for runtime, but error messages indicate incompatibility.

2) Inside container (launched with --gpus all):
$ docker run --gpus all --rm -it my-inference-image:latest bash\# inside:
root@c1:/# python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())"
2.2.0 True False
# also saw runtime error:
RuntimeError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version

3) LDD on libcuda.so from inside container:
root@c1:/# ldconfig -p | grep libcuda
libcuda.so.1 (libc6,x86-64) => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1
root@c1:/# ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 14 Feb 12  2024 /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 -> cuda/lib64/libcuda.so.1
# But /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/cuda/lib64 doesn't exist inside container (bind mount mismatch).

4) Check libcuda version against driver with strings:
$ strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 | head -n 5
__cudaRegisterFatBinary
__cudaUnregisterFatBinary
CUDA Version: 11.7.0
# shows CUDA Version: 11.7 in the binary linked inside container, mismatch to host driver (12.x).

5) dmesg/gpu kernel messages when starting containerized runtime:
[  +0.000000] nvidia: module license 'NVIDIA' taints kernel.
[  +0.010000] nvidia 0000:01:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  +0.002000] NVRM: Xid (GPU 0000:01:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
# Xid 79 often correlates to ECC/driver issues or kernel panic in driver stack.

6) Reproduced OOM-ish stack during model allocation:
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.23 GiB (GPU 0; 24.00 GiB total capacity; 22.50 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free)
# But top-level stats show <1 GiB used prior to this call. Possible stale allocation accounting due to driver mismatch.

ATTEMPTED FIXES (and results):
- Reinstalled nvidia-driver 525 -> rebooted host -> nvidia-smi ok. Container still intermittently says driver insufficient.
- Verified nvidia-container-toolkit v1.11.0, reinstalled toolkit, restarted docker. No change.
- Mounted /usr/lib/nvidia-*/ and /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu into container to ensure libcuda visible -> changed error to different symbols missing.
- Tried forcing LD_LIBRARY_PATH inside container to host libs: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH -> sometimes fixes runtime errors but causes ABI mismatch crashes.
- Switched conda cudatoolkit from 11.7 to 12.1 in a clean env, reinstalled torch wheel for cu121 (not officially distributed for this OS) -> container reported libtorch CUDA symbol mismatch.
- On WSL2 laptop, replaced driver with 535 nightly -> caused kernel crash. Rolled back.

HYPOTHESES / NOTES:
- Two separate mismatch axes cause issues: 1) host kernel driver <-> container exposed libcuda.so linking mismatch, and 2) Python wheel (torch built for cu117) expects matching runtime symbols. If libcuda inside container does not match device driver, torch runtime can detect insufficient driver.
- Host driver claiming CUDA 12.1 while libcuda in container identifies as 11.7 suggests stale bind mount or symlink that points at an older shipped libcuda in the image. Some base images (nvidia/cuda:11.7-runtime) include libcuda shim that may conflict with host bind.
- OOM errors with incorrect reporting numbers often indicate driver/kernel mismatch rather than true memory exhaustion. Xid 79 and "GPU has fallen off the bus" point at driver instability.

QUICK REPRO / CHECKLIST (for next time):
1) On host: sudo dmesg | grep -i nvrm / grep -i nvidia -> capture Xid codes.
2) nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version --format=csv
3) Inside container: python -c "import ctypes; print(ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1'))" to see if loader can open the same library.
4) ldconfig -p | grep libcuda and readlink -f on the returned path to confirm it actually points to host driver files exposed into container.
5) Check docker run flags: ensure --gpus all and not mounting an older CUDA toolkit into container root. Avoid copying host /usr/local/cuda into image.
6) Test with official nvidia/cuda:12.1-runtime base image and matching torch wheel (if available).
7) When in doubt, remove in-image libcuda, rely solely on host-provided libcuda via nvidia container runtime.

NEXT STEPS / ACTIONS TO TRY:
- Rebuild minimal repro image starting from nvidia/cuda:12.1-runtime and minimal python; avoid bundling any libcuda-related files. Install wheel built for cu121 (or use cpu fallback to validate server binary).
- Add diagnostic startup script in image that prints: nvidia-smi, ldconfig -p | grep libcuda, readlink -f $(which libcuda.so.1 || true), python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())". Log this to /tmp/gpu-diagnostics.txt on startup to capture host vs container discrepancy.
- For desktop: try rolling back to driver 520.x (known stable for this CUDA/toolkit mix) in a spare test environment to see if Xid errors go away.
- Open ticket JIRA-5482 with kernel dmesg and docker diagnostic output attached (TODO: attach).

RANDOM NOTES / reminders:
- Watch out for conda cudatoolkit: it is not the same as system driver. conda only provides user-space runtime libs; kernel driver must support it.
- If you see "libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file" inside container, check that you didn't accidentally install the full CUDA toolkit in the image and then mounted a different libcuda at runtime.
- NCCL warnings often happen early and are unrelated to memory; focus on Xid and driver mismatch first.
- If reproducible on CI, try using plain CPU build to isolate memory bug vs driver problem.

Scratchpad done for now. TODO: run the minimal repro, attach logs to JIRA, ping Samir for kernel logs.
